# POSITION SOURCE FAMILIES — every figure queried, every grain named

*Generated 2026-09-04T00:12:59.579Z by `npm run report:position-sources -- --write`.*
*Do not edit this file. Regenerate it.*

## Why this file exists

SURFACE 3 §0a. A source-family table drawn from sprint reports is a set of numbers
that were true on the day each report was written, carried forward as if they were
properties of the system. **An inference must not travel as a measurement.**

⚠⚠ **The disagreement this was written to settle is not a contradiction — it is a
grain error, and both numbers are correct.** `members-interests` names a corpus of
documents, a set of graph edges and a set of position signals, and they are three
different sizes because they count three different things. Quoting any one as "the
interests we hold" is true of one grain and false of the other two. **Every row below
states its grain in the row.**

⚠ `SEARCH_TO_LEX_POSITION_SOURCES.md` **does not exist in this repository** — not on
disk, not tracked, and not in the history of any ref. It could not be marked
superseded because there is nothing to mark. This file is what it should have been.

## `vote` — votes in recorded divisions

| grain (what ONE row is) | where it lives | n | note |
|---|---|---:|---|
| a division | `divisions` | 5,645 | one row per division of either House |
| a member’s vote | `division_votes` | 2,129,113 | aye/no only; tellers and absences are not votes |
| a signal | `position_signal_vote (view, derived)` | 2,080,585 | ⚠ DERIVED, never stored. A vote becomes a signal only where the member resolves to a graph entity, so this is BELOW the vote count and the gap is unresolved members |

⚠ **How these reconcile.** A division CONTAINS many votes, so the first two rows go UP, not down — these grains are not nested and no "percentage surviving" is meaningful across them. The only step that loses anything is the last: 2,129,113 votes become 2,080,585 signals (97.7%), and the 48,528 missing are votes cast by members who do not resolve to a graph entity.

## `declared_interest` — interests declared in the register

| grain (what ONE row is) | where it lives | n | note |
|---|---|---:|---|
| a published interest | `interests-api.parliament.uk` | 4,100 | ⚠⚠ NOT A QUERY. This is the census reading of 2026-08-27 (docs/census/members-interests.json, published_units) and it is the ONLY figure in this table that is not live. It is the publisher’s own total, unreachable from here without an API call, and it is labelled rather than omitted because the gap between it and the row below is the coverage story |
| a held document | `corpus_sections (members-interests)` | 3,448 | ⚠⚠ THIS IS THE 3,448 THAT CIRCULATES AS "the interests we hold". It is a count of DOCUMENTS IN THE SEARCH CORPUS, marked excluded-by-design for retrieval, and it is not the number of interests the position graph can use |
| an edge | `graph_edge (declared-interest)` | 1,505 | the entity-resolved relationship |
| a signal | `position_signal_stored` | 1,723 | ⚠ what the position graph actually reasons over |

⚠ **How these reconcile.** ⚠⚠ THERE ARE MORE SIGNALS THAN EDGES, AND THAT IS A GRAIN DIFFERENCE RATHER THAN A FAULT. The edge table is deduplicated to one row per (member, organisation) PAIR; the signal layer is DATED. Measured: the signals cover 1,505 distinct pairs against 1,505 edges, and 1,723 distinct (member, organisation, date) triples, which is exactly the signal count. A member who declared the same interest in two different years is ONE edge and TWO signals. **So none of these four numbers is "the interests we hold" — they are four different questions, and the corpus row is not even about the position graph.**

## `witness_appearance` — appearances as a witness before a committee inquiry

| grain (what ONE row is) | where it lives | n | note |
|---|---|---:|---|
| an edge | `graph_edge (gave-evidence-to)` | 162,733 | one row per witness per inquiry appearance |
| a signal | `position_signal_stored` | 175,290 | what the position graph reasons over |

⚠ **How these reconcile.** The same grain difference as interests, and here it is exact: the signals cover 162,733 distinct (witness, inquiry) pairs against 162,733 edges (identical), and 175,290 distinct (witness, inquiry, date) triples, which is exactly the signal count. A witness who appeared before one inquiry on three days is ONE edge and THREE signals.

## `political_donation` — donations in the Electoral Commission register

| grain (what ONE row is) | where it lives | n | note |
|---|---|---:|---|
| a published donation | `position_donation` | 89,861 | every row the Commission publishes that we ingested |
| a donation with BOTH ends resolved | `position_donation` | 251 | ⚠⚠ THE ONLY ROWS THAT CAN BECOME A SIGNAL. Quoting the row above as the register’s yield is the mistake SURFACE 3 §3 corrects |
| a signal | `position_signal_stored` | 244 | grouped to (member, donor, date), so several donations on one day are one signal |

⚠ **How these reconcile.** ⚠⚠ The collapse is at the RESOLUTION step, not the grouping step: of 89,861 published donations only 251 have BOTH a resolved donor and a resolved recipient, and those group to 244 signals. Any prediction that scales the signal count by growth in DONOR-resolved rows alone is using the wrong denominator — see SURFACE 3 §3.
